summary: Reviewed the FORGE-BOARD-7 branch (forge sanitise + three hygiene primitives + update-triggered health cadence + docs) against the actual code. Correctness verified: sanitise exit-code semantics are right (--check counts every issue and mutates nothing; plain run applies only the safe fixes and exits nonzero iff an UNRESOLVED issue remains); the fix-vs-report boundary matches the honesty rule (only roadmap heal-on-drift and tracked-cruft git-rm-cached are auto-applied, everything needing judgment is reported). Refactors are behaviour-preserving: check_repo_budget's tracked_cruft globs select the same realistic set as the old substring filter; intake.stale_task_state is a pure reporter and the sole unlink stays in the human-gated --discard-active path; _roadmap_drift's duplicates>0 test is complete because heal_items only dedupes by key. Tests are comprehensive: 8 new tests pin each invariant (fix-vs-report, --check read-only, never-deletes-evidence, secret/cruft scan, stale-reports-not-clears, mode-abandon, harness-health-no-cron, skill registration).

non_blocking_findings.summary: tracked_cruft() raises a raw CalledProcessError on git failure, unlike the sibling git calls routed through _git_paths then fail(); on a broken repo sanitise would traceback instead of failing cleanly.
in --check mode the issue_count term len(resolved) is always zero because fixes are skipped, so adding it is a harmless no-op.
